title: Picture Series
source: MindSpark Grade 4 Aptitude & Reasoning | Chapter 3: Picture Series
subtopics: Picture series by count (number of objects increases or decreases)
Picture series by shading (empty to filled)
Picture series by rotation (shape turns each step)
Picture series by size (growing or shrinking)
Picture series by adding or removing parts
learningGoals: Track ONE attribute at a time to find the rule in a picture series.
Predict what comes next in a visual pattern.
Describe the rule in words: 'Each step, the shape...'
coreIdeas: Look at ONE thing at a time — count, shading, rotation, or size.
Turn what you see into a simple number pattern to find the rule.
The next picture in the series must follow the SAME rule every step.

workedExamples.problem: Box 1: one star. Box 2: two stars. Box 3: three stars. Box 4: __ stars.
workedExamples.solution: The count goes up by 1 each box. Rule: add 1 star. Box 4 will have four stars.

workedExamples.problem: Box 1: circle (empty). Box 2: circle (half shaded). Box 3: circle (fully shaded). Box 4: square (empty). What is Box 5?
workedExamples.solution: Shading resets every 3 boxes AND the shape changes. Box 5 = square (half shaded).

workedExamples.problem: An arrow points UP. Next it points RIGHT. Next it points DOWN. Next it points LEFT. What comes next?
workedExamples.solution: The arrow rotates 90° clockwise each step. After LEFT comes UP again — it is a cycle of 4.

onboarding.coachIntro: Spark the coach opens Picture Series by showing a simple count pattern (1 dot, 2 dots, 3 dots) and asks: 'What comes in the next box?' to prove the idea instantly. Then Spark teaches the 'track one thing at a time' strategy before exercises begin.
onboarding.placementRule: Start at Group A for all learners. If two consecutive wrong answers in Groups A–B, slow down and describe the attribute changing step by step before trying again.

mission.missionPromise: By the end, you will look at any picture series and spot the changing rule in seconds — like reading a visual comic strip!
mission.successCelebration: Award a badge pulse and coach cheer after every correct group. At lesson end, show 'Visual Genius' trophy.

microLessonPattern: Coach opens with a visual hook — a partially drawn series on the board.
Coach tracks one attribute out loud and converts it to a number.
Coach reads the practice question and describes each picture.
Student picks the next picture in the series.
Instant feedback explains the rule clearly if wrong.
Review question confirms mastery before the next group.

rewardLoop.xpUnit: Award 10 to 20 XP per exercise group.
rewardLoop.streakRule: Show streak counter; protect with one free retry before streak breaks.
rewardLoop.badgeRule: Each group unlocks one badge tied to the attribute type.
rewardLoop.celebrationStyle: Quick coach praise + XP pulse + progress rail tick after every correct answer.

reviewLoop.trigger: Two incorrect attempts triggers a mini-reteach by writing the numeric version of the visual pattern.
reviewLoop.practiceStyle: Offer a simpler version with only one obvious change.
reviewLoop.masteryRule: Advance only after correct answer plus description of the rule.
reviewLoop.revisitRule: Any group with two errors returns at the next session.

uiDirectives.noScrollGoal: Mission progress, question, and action buttons visible without scrolling.

beats.teacherLine: Hello, visual superstar! Welcome to Picture Series — where pictures tell a story and YOU figure out what comes next! Every picture series has a rule. Something changes in the same way every single step. It could be the COUNT of things, the SHADING, the SIZE, or the DIRECTION. Your special trick: track ONE thing at a time. Turn what you see into a number and you will crack the rule instantly!
beats.boardAction: Draw 3 boxes in a row. Box 1: one circle. Box 2: two circles. Box 3: three circles. Then draw a blank 4th box with a question mark. Write '1 → 2 → 3 → ?' below.
beats.checkpointPrompt: Quick warm-up: Box 1 has 1 dot, Box 2 has 2 dots, Box 3 has 3 dots — how many dots will Box 4 have?
beats.fallbackHint: The count goes 1, 2, 3 — adding 1 each time. So Box 4 will have 1 more: 3 + 1 = 4 dots!

svgAnimation.text: Track ONE thing: count / shading / size / direction

beats.teacherLine: Let me demonstrate the shading trick! Box 1: an empty triangle. Box 2: triangle with the bottom half shaded. Box 3: triangle fully shaded. I write the shading as numbers: 0, half, full — that is 0, 1, 2. The rule is 'add one layer of shading each step'. So Box 4 resets back to empty (start a new shape or cycle back). Easy once you see the number pattern hidden in the shading!
beats.boardAction: Draw three triangles: empty, half-shaded, fully shaded. Below each write 0, 1, 2. Arrow showing +1. Then draw Box 4 with an empty square (reset/new shape) and explain the cycle.
beats.checkpointPrompt: Your turn: Picture 1 = small star, Picture 2 = medium star, Picture 3 = large star — describe the rule and what Picture 4 will look like.
beats.expectedStudentResponse: The star grows each step; Picture 4 will be an extra-large star.
beats.fallbackHint: The size goes small → medium → large. The rule is 'get one size bigger each step'. So Picture 4 is an extra-large star!

svgAnimation.text: Rule: add one shading level each step!

beats.teacherLine: You have the visual toolkit! Remember: count, shading, size, direction — track ONE at a time. Work through Groups A to F. Describe what you see before you answer. Ready? Let's finish those picture stories!
beats.boardAction: Show a cheatsheet: Attribute → Convert to number → Find rule → Apply to next step. List the 4 attributes: Count, Shading (0=empty, 1=half, 2=full), Size (S/M/L), Direction (U/R/D/L).
beats.checkpointPrompt: Quick check: if an arrow points Up in Step 1 and Right in Step 2 — which direction does it rotate each step?
beats.expectedStudentResponse: Clockwise — it turns 90° to the right each step.
beats.fallbackHint: Up → Right is a quarter-turn clockwise. That is 90° to the right. If the same rule continues, Right → Down next.

svgAnimation.text: Rotation: Up → Right → Down → Left → Up ...

sessionFlow.missionStepTitle: Exercise A: Counting Up in Pictures
sessionFlow.coachHook: Let's figure this out together! Count the objects in each box. The number tells the story!

boardDemo.title: Count Pattern in Pictures
steps: Box 1: 2 apples, Box 2: 4 apples, Box 3: 6 apples
boardDemo.teacherLine: Write the count under each box as a number. Now you have a number pattern — find the rule and apply it to the next box!

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Box 1: 1 flower. Box 2: 2 flowers. Box 3: 3 flowers. Box 4: __ flowers. What is the count pattern?
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Your turn: Box 1 = 5 dots, Box 2 = 10 dots, Box 3 = 15 dots, Box 4 = __ dots. How many?
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Yes! 5, 10, 15 — adding 5 each time. Box 4 = 15 + 5 = 20 dots!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: write the counts: 5, 10, 15. Subtract: 10 − 5 = 5. The rule is +5. So 15 + 5 = 20.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Quick: Box 1 = 3 stars, Box 2 = 6 stars, Box 3 = 9 stars. What is Box 4?

sessionFlow.coachHook: Let's figure this out together! Watch the shading — is the shape getting more filled or less filled each step?

boardDemo.title: Shading Pattern — Filling Up
steps: Rule: add one quarter of shading each step
boardDemo.teacherLine: Think of shading as filling a glass with water. Each step adds more. How much is added each time? That is your rule!

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Picture 1 = empty circle. Picture 2 = half-shaded circle. Picture 3 = fully shaded circle. Picture 4 = empty circle (new). What is happening?
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Your turn: Picture 1 = empty box. Picture 2 = half-shaded box. Picture 3 = __ (what comes next in the shading)?
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Exactly! Empty → half → full. The shading grows step by step. Picture 3 is fully shaded!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: empty is 0, half is 1, full is 2. Pattern: 0, 1, 2 — adding 1 each step. After 1 (half) comes 2 (full).
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Quick: if the shading goes full → half → empty, what is the rule and what comes after empty?

sessionFlow.coachHook: Let's figure this out together! The shape is turning like the hands of a clock. Find out which direction and how far each step!

boardDemo.title: Rotation Pattern — Quarter Turns
steps: Step 5: Arrow pointing UP again (full cycle)
boardDemo.teacherLine: Think of a clock: 12 o'clock, 3 o'clock, 6 o'clock, 9 o'clock. A 90° clockwise turn moves the same way. After 4 steps it comes back to the start — it is a cycle of 4!

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: An arrow: Step 1 points Right, Step 2 points Down, Step 3 points Left, Step 4 = ? Which direction?
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Your turn: Letter L is upright in Step 1. It is rotated 90° clockwise in Step 2 (looks like an upside-down T). Step 3 = rotated another 90° clockwise. What does Step 3 look like?
sessionFlow.masteryCheck: L rotated 180° — it looks like an upside-down L (pointing up-left)
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Brilliant! Each step is a 90° clockwise turn. Two steps = 180°. The L flips upside down. Great visualising!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: one 90° clockwise turn is like turning a page to the right. After two 90° turns, the shape is completely upside down — rotated 180°.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Quick: a triangle pointing UP rotates 90° clockwise each step. Step 1=UP, Step 2=RIGHT, Step 3=DOWN, Step 4=?

sessionFlow.coachHook: Let's figure this out together! The shape is changing size each step. Is it growing or shrinking? By how much?

boardDemo.title: Size Pattern — Getting Bigger
steps: Rule: side length increases by 1 each step
boardDemo.teacherLine: Label the size as Small, Medium, Large, Extra Large or use 1, 2, 3, 4. Find the step — does it go up by 1 size or jump by 2? Then apply the same step to the next box.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Picture 1: tiny circle. Picture 2: small circle. Picture 3: medium circle. Picture 4: __ circle. What size comes next?
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Your turn: the shape goes Large → Medium → Small. What comes after Small?
sessionFlow.masteryCheck: Tiny (extra-small) — the shape is shrinking one size each step.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Correct! Large → Medium → Small → Tiny. Each step shrinks by one size. Great pattern reading!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: the shape is getting smaller each step. Large is 3, Medium is 2, Small is 1. What comes after 1? Zero — so Tiny (the smallest possible).

sessionFlow.subtopic: Picture series by adding or removing parts
sessionFlow.missionStepTitle: Exercise E: Parts Added or Removed
sessionFlow.coachHook: Let's figure this out together! Each step, a new part appears — or one disappears. Count the parts and find the rule!

boardDemo.title: Parts Pattern — Building a Shape
steps: Step 1: a square with 0 dots inside
Step 2: a square with 1 dot inside
Step 3: a square with 2 dots inside
Step 4: a square with 3 dots inside
boardDemo.teacherLine: Count the parts (dots, lines, shapes inside) for each picture. Write those counts as a number series. Now you have a normal number pattern to solve!

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Step 1: a triangle with 1 line inside. Step 2: triangle with 2 lines inside. Step 3: triangle with 3 lines inside. Step 4: __ lines inside?
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Your turn: a star starts with 5 points. Each step, one point is removed. Step 1 = 5 points, Step 2 = 4 points, Step 3 = 3 points. Step 4 = __ points?
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Spot on! 5 → 4 → 3 → 2. Subtracting 1 point each step. You tracked those parts perfectly!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: count the points at each step: 5, 4, 3. That is minus 1 each time. So 3 − 1 = 2 points in Step 4.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Quick: Step 1 = 2 petals, Step 2 = 4 petals, Step 3 = 6 petals. How many petals in Step 4?

sessionFlow.missionStepTitle: Exercise F: Two Things Change at Once!
sessionFlow.coachHook: Let's figure this out together — this is the challenge round! Two things change at the same time. Track each one separately, then combine!

boardDemo.title: Mixed Pattern — Two Attributes
steps: Attribute 2 (shading): empty → half → full (+1 shading level)
Box 4: extra-large fully shaded circle (size resets or continues; shading resets to empty)
boardDemo.teacherLine: Split the problem into two simpler ones. Handle size alone. Handle shading alone. Solve each, then describe the next picture with both answers combined!

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Picture 1: tiny UP-arrow. Picture 2: medium RIGHT-arrow. Picture 3: large DOWN-arrow. What is Picture 4 — describe the size AND direction!
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Your turn: Box 1 = 1 red star, Box 2 = 2 blue stars, Box 3 = 3 red stars. Box 4 = __ stars and what colour?
sessionFlow.masteryCheck: 4 blue stars — count adds 1 each step; colour alternates red/blue/red/blue.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Amazing! Count: 1,2,3,4 (+1 each step). Colour: red,blue,red,blue (alternating). Box 4 = 4 blue stars! You cracked a two-attribute series!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: cover the colour, just count: 1,2,3 → next is 4. Now cover the count, just look at colour: red,blue,red — it alternates! After red comes blue. So: 4 blue stars.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Final: Box 1 = small triangle, Box 2 = medium square, Box 3 = large pentagon. What shape and size is Box 4?
